_provenance.classification: Membership in the real gate decides first (_resolved_sites asks CoverageGenerator.citations_for itself, so no hole can open between the two gates and no predicate is copied). A GATED site is then also guarded here when foreign content survives removing its 8.4 tokens - that is what covers the 9 mixed sites, static and dynamic alike. Classifying by content first discarded every gated dynamic site wholesale, which left the foreign half of D-38 own clamp citation f'5.2.6.3.(1); {prefix}.1.(2)' deletable with nothing moving.
_provenance.key_stability: Dynamic keys come from ast.get_source_segment, validated by re-parsing: the slice is used only when it rebuilds the same tree, else a structural ast.dump is the fallback. ast.unparse cannot be used - it re-renders in the running interpreter syntax, so an f-string key authored on 3.12 (PEP 701) is not the key 3.11 emits. That shipped in the first revision and CI 3.11 job caught it; the floor is requires-python >=3.11.
_provenance.populations: Exact physical-site accounting at 2026-09-18: 278 article= sites in python/btap/**/*.py; 105 resolve onto a Section 8.4 article and are covered by citation_counts_baseline.json; 173 sit entirely outside that gate (173/278 = 62 percent); 9 are MIXED, citing both an 8.4 article and something else. This baseline covers the 173 plus the 9 mixed = 182, so the two baselines overlap on 9 sites BY DESIGN and must not be read as disjoint. An earlier revision said 105 and 178 as though they were, and the revision before that compared the 8.4 gate per-EDITION total of 213 (96 for 2020 plus 117 for 2025, of those same 105 sites) against a per-site figure, which understated the gap as 45 percent.
_provenance.rebaseline_reason: Re-baselined for Sol's `114`.4. The specific multi-energy entry cited the (6)(b) SUBCLAUSE, which asserts a capacity band: (6)(b) is at or below 176 kW, (6)(c) covers 176-352 and (6)(d) above. Which applies depends on the REFERENCE plant's heating capacity, which does not exist at selection time, so no subclause could be established. The citation is now the sentence, built as f'{ratio_article}; {sentence_six}', which REPLACES the f'{ratio_article}; {boiler_article}' key of the previous re-baseline: one dynamic key retires and one appears, the count is unchanged, and nothing is lost. The generic entry's lone `ratio_article` key is untouched.
_provenance.why: DF-15. The 8.4 gate counts a citation only if its literal resolves onto an article in that edition articles_8_4.json, and _scan_citations drops a non-8.4 literal at SCAN time before that, so those citations could be deleted without failing anything. Not all 182 are Part 4/5/6: about 20 are variables bound to 8.4 f-strings and three are the data-driven coverage emitter in btap/audit, so the honest description is sites the 8.4 scanner cannot count. This baseline does NOT widen the coverage attestation, which is a Section 8.4 document. PRIOR REBASELINE: Re-baselined for the D-100 envelope review's edition-owned citation fix. Two hard-coded NECB 2020 literals were replaced by ruleset.article() lookups, so their literal counts drop to zero by design: 'Table 3.2.2.2.; 3.1.1.7.(4)' in envelope/prescriptive.py and the Note 'A-8.4.4.4.(1)' inside reference.py's thermal-mass citation. Article 3.1.1.7 keeps its number across editions but was restructured from eight sentences to four, so the enclosure credit moved 2020 (4) -> 2025 (3) and inclination moved 2020 (6) -> 2025 (4); the literal cited the wrong sentence on every 2025 run and never cited inclination at all. The thermal-mass Note moved A-8.4.4.4.(1) -> A-8.4.5.4.(1). Citations are not lost: they are now resolved per edition and BOTH clauses are emitted, which the static literal scanner cannot see. PRIOR REBASELINE: Re-baselined for the multi-energy disclosure's edition-resolved citations (Sol, `113`). The warning's article was a hardcoded '8.4.4.9.(5); 8.4.4.9.(6)(b)' literal, which cited 2020's numbers to the AHJ on every necb2025 run. It now derives both from the ruleset via multi_energy_articles(selection), exactly as heat_pump_article_base already does for the same defect, so the two sites become DYNAMIC and leave the static scanner — the documented trade-off in that helper's docstring: the articles stay declared in the article_coverage manifests, and citing the wrong number is worse than citing fewer times. Two dynamic sites added (the dual-fuel-plant entry citing both sentences and the generic entry citing the ratio sentence alone); the static warn count for 8.4.4.9/8.4.5.9 returns to its pre-change value, so citation_counts_baseline.json needs no change at all.
